name: Owlfolk
body:
Owlfolk are a peaceful species of avian humanoids known for their great love of learning. They are most commonly found near human, elven, and other humanoid settlements, where they can often be found working as merchants, scholars, and librarians.

Physical

Distant kin of birdfolk, owlfolk come in many shapes and sizes, from petite and fluffy to wide-winged and majestic. Their downy feathers muffle sound and range in color from darkest black to snow white, with many bearing striated camouflage patterns that help them blend into natural terrain.

Like birdfolk, owlfolk’s wings are part of their arms, preventing them from flying and wielding objects at the same time. Owlfolk are silent but unsophisticated flyers, and usually hover not far from the ground, unlike their sky-loving birdfolk cousins.

Owlfolk find modern humanoid fashion to their liking, always taking the necessary steps to let out the sleeves of their garments so that they can spread their wings properly.

Social

Most owlfolk are urban or operate small family farms. While some live in small, remote enclaves consisting only of owlfolk, this is usually done only out of necessity.

Most are very cosmopolitan and prefer regions where many species and ethnicities are present, as these areas ted to have the best opportunities for learning. Owlfolk are particularly interested in magic, and many can be found as pupils or students at magical academies.

Owlfolk find humans, halflings, gnomes, half-elves, and elves delightful. They tolerate dwarves ratfolk, and the better-behaved kobolds and goblins, but are intimidated around orcs and half-orcs.

Alignment and Religion

Overall, owlfolk lean toward Chaotic Good, although their preference or neither Good nor Chaos is particularly strong. The lust for knowledge drives many of them more than ethical considerations, and this temptation may tempt some of them towards Evil.

Likewise, while most have a penchant for autonomy, many spend a long time in one place find themselves developing a sense of communal belonging that may them drift toward the traditionalism of Lawful alignments.

Owlfolk have no particular overarching religious philosophy, and usually follow the practices of whatever larger community they are a part of—if they are religious at all.

Names

Owlfolk names are just as likely to be in Common as they are to be in Aurin. Typical owlfolk names include (choose or roll 1d20):

Akoot
Billywix
Hoho
Honour
Hooper
Hootie
Kodo
Kuko
Kwidi
Luma
Okeyo
Pelly
Quisp
Rikiloo
Shimmer
Thrasher
Townsdale
Trixie
Whit
Willy
Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are undersized physically, but mentally sharp and wise beyond your years. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Int, +2 Wis, –2 Str [specialized]. (1)
Size As a Small creature, you have a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a +1 size bonus to your Armor Class, a –1 size penalty to your CMB, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks. You must use smaller weapons than Medium creatures. As a Small creature, you occupy a space of 5 feet by 5 feet. Your reach is 5 feet. (0)
Type Humanoid. You are a Humanoid with the owlfolk subtype. (0)
Speed Slow. Your base speed is 20 feet. (–1)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Aurin. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any language except for secret languages. (1)
Other Species Traits
Senses Darkvision. You have darkvision 60 feet. (2)
Flight (Ex) Your arms double as wings, allowing you to fly with a speed of 30 feet (clumsy maneuverability). You cannot fly while wearing medium or heavy armor, or while carrying a heavy load. (4)
Senses Low-light vision. You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions. (1)
Stealthy Your feathers absorb light and muffle sound. You gain a +2 species bonus on Stealth checks. (2)
Total: 10 RP (standard)
Variants
Groundling

You come from a long-line of owlfolk whose wings were underdeveloped, but who developed ground-based survival strategies to compensate.

Ground Speed Your base speed is 30 feet and you gain a burrow speed of 15 feet. This trait alters speed and replaces flight.
Ground Survivor You gain a +2 species bonus to Survival checks. This trait replaces stealthy.
Alternate Species Traits
Academician You gain a +2 bonus on any single Knowledge skill. This trait replaces stealthy.
Gift of Tongues You gain a +1 species bonus on Bluff and Diplomacy checks, and you learn one additional language every time you put a rank in the Linguistics skill. This trait replaces stealthy.
Heavy Wings Your wings are not capable of flight, but you can glide—taking no damage from a fall (as if subject to a constant non-magical feather fall spell). In addition, the talons on your hands are heavier than most owlfolk, allowing you to make two claw attacks. These are primary natural attacks that deal 1d3 damage each. This trait replaces flight and stealthy.
Inscrutable You gain a +2 species bonus on Bluff checks. This trait replaces stealthy.
Night Hunter You gain a +4 species bonus on Stealth checks made in areas of dim light or darkness. This trait replaces stealthy.
Stoic Compared to most owlfolk, you are more focused on your personal goals than on your studies. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Dex, +2 Con, –2 Cha. This trait alters ability score modifiers.
Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist Add +1 extract formula from the alchemist list to your formula book. This formula must be at least one level below the highest-level alchemist formula you can create.
Arcanist Add +1 spell from the arcanist spell list to your spellbook. This spell must be at least 1 spell level lower than the highest-level arcanist spell you can cast.
Bard Add +1/2 to your bardic knowledge bonus.
Cleric Select one domain power granted at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Wisdom modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that domain power.
Fighter Add a +1/2 bonus on Bluff checks to feint and Diplomacy checks to gather information.
Friar Add +1 to your total number of evangelization rounds per day.
Gunslinger Add +1/4 to the dodge bonus to AC granted by the nimble class feature (maximum +4).
Investigator Add +1 extract formula from the investigator list to your formula book. This formula must be at least one level below the highest-level investigator formula you can create.
Magus Add +1 spell from the magus spell list to your spellbook. This spell must be at least 1 spell level lower than the highest-level magus spell you can cast.
Monk Add +1/3 to your AC bonus monk class ability.
Occultist Add +1/2 point of mental focus per day.
Oracle Add a +1/2 bonus to Knowledge (history) and Knowledge (planes) checks.
Psychic Add +1 spell from the psychic spell list to your known spells. This spell must be at least 1 spell level lower than the highest-level psychic spell you can cast.
Ranger Add a +1/2 bonus on Perception checks made in dim light or darkness.
Rogue Gain a +1/2 bonus on Disable Device and Use Magic Device checks related to glyphs, symbols, scrolls, and other magical writings.
Scholar Gain +1/5 of a new basic study.
Sorcerer Select one bloodline power at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that bloodline power.
Summoner Add +1 spell from the summoner spell list to your known spells. This spell must be at least 1 spell level lower than the highest-level summoner spell you can cast.
Witch Add +1 spell from the witch spell list to your familiar. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level witch spell you can cast. If you ever replace your familiar, the new familiar knows these bonus spells.
Wizard Add +1 spell from the wizard spell list to your spellbook. This spell must be at least 1 spell level lower than the highest-level wizard spell you can cast.
